svg.aria-label: The tests were green. The bugs were still there. A map of an app that adopted bkit, in four columns: screens (web and phone), API, services and outside services, with thin lines for the calls between them. Red circles mark what bkit's audit templates found, bigger for bigger problems. Testing audit: tests that could never fail, about 100 of which read the code as text instead of running it; a security hole, where a sign-in link could send people to another website; no test made a request fail, so a failed save could still show “Saved”; a fix in dead code, while the live screen next to it stayed broken; phone tests that weren't, with 23 of 33 actually running as web pages. Duplication audit: one rule written 8 times, whose copies drifted so some billed accounts users had left; one database read in 4 copies, word for word, one inside the API itself. This map used 2 of the 35 audit templates bkit ships: Accessibility, Adoption, Agents, AI search & SEO, Analytics, Annotations, App performance, App Store, Architecture, CI performance, Config, Cost, Coverage, Database, Dead code, Deferrals, Dependencies, Documentation, Duplication, Failures, Flaky tests, Gates, Issues, LLM, Logs, Models, Privacy, Prompts, Red team, Reliability, Repo, Security, Slop, Testing, Usability.
